text: Plants make their own food. They use light from the sun, water from the soil and air. This is called photosynthesis. The green parts of a plant, the leaves, do most of the work. The plant makes sugar and gives out oxygen. Animals and people need that oxygen to breathe. So plants help all living things on Earth.

The water cycle is how water moves around our planet. The sun heats water in seas and lakes, and it goes up into the air. High in the sky, the water gets cold and makes clouds. When the clouds get heavy, rain or snow falls. The water flows back into rivers and seas. Then it all starts again.

A fraction shows a part of a whole. If you cut a pizza into four equal pieces and eat one, you ate one fourth of the pizza. The top number tells how many parts you have. The bottom number tells how many equal parts make the whole. Two fourths is the same as one half.

Our bodies have bones that hold us up. An adult has about two hundred bones. The skull keeps the brain safe. The ribs keep the heart and lungs safe. Muscles pull on the bones so we can move. To keep bones strong, eat good food, drink milk and play outside every day.

Long ago, people did not have paper. They wrote on clay, stone and animal skins. Later, people in China made paper from plants. It was light and easy to carry. Paper helped people share stories and ideas. Today we still use paper, but we also read and write on screens.

Magnets pull on some metals, like iron. Every magnet has two ends, called poles. One is the north pole and one is the south pole. Two different poles pull toward each other. Two poles that are the same push away. The Earth is like a big magnet, and that is why a compass points north.

Volcanoes are openings in the ground where hot rock comes out. Deep under the Earth, it is so hot that rock melts. When this melted rock comes up, we call it lava. Some volcanoes are quiet for a long time. Others erupt often. People who study volcanoes help keep towns safe.
